paragraphs.text: A most sharp reprehension, because, while they despise the apostle's admonitions, they tempt Christ's own patience: and also while they condemn him as wretched and miserable, they lay nothing against him, which is not common to him with Christ.

paragraphs.text: And will be most mighty to be avenged upon you, when need will be.
paragraphs.label: a

paragraphs.text: Regarding that base form of a servant which he took upon him when he abased himself.
paragraphs.label: b

paragraphs.text: He confirms that which he spoke about the power of God appearing in his ministry, and he gathers by the mutual relation between the people's faith and the minister's preaching, that they must either reverence his apostleship, upon whose doctrine their faith is grounded, or they must condemn themselves of infidelity, and must confess themselves not to be of Christ's body.

He appeases that sharpness, trusting that they will show themselves towards their faithful apostle, able and willing to be taught. And he also adds this, that he does not seek his own fame and estimation, so that they may serve their saviour, which is the only mark that he shoots at.
paragraphs.anchor: But I trust that ye shall

paragraphs.text: That all things may be in good order among you, and the members of the church restored into their place, which have been shaken and are out of place.
paragraphs.label: d

paragraphs.text: A brief exhortation, but yet such a one as comprehends all the parts of a Christian man's life.
He salutes them familiarly, and in conclusion wishes well to them.
